entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava

--------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Sheo Kumar Singh, Advocate.
For the State : Mr. Prabir Kumar Chatterjee @ Prabir Chatterjee, A.P.P.
---------
th Order No. 03/Dated: 12 June, 2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner has been made an accused in connection with Ketar P.S. Case No. 11 of 2024 registered for the offence under Sections 414, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of the I.P.C. and Under Sections 4(1)A and 21 of the Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act., pending in the Court of learned Court of S.D.J.M., Nagar Untari, Garhwa.
As per FIR, allegation is that the petitioner was carrying illegal coal which was made with an accident having Registration No. UP-64T-9516.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all as alleged in this case,
Hence, petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case.
Petitioner is in custody since 17.03.2024 and allegation against the petitioner is that while driving Truck No. UP64AT-9516 loaded with 29 tonn coal and met with an accident.
Therefore, vehicle was seized.
Petitioner has produced all the documents as well as the purchased of the coal and its valid transports.
Now, Charge sheet has been submitted.
Petitioner has no criminal background.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.

On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submitted that there are Page 1|2 sufficient materials against the petitioner showing his involvement in the present case.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve bail.

Regarding being had to the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation coupled with the materials available against the petitioner, I am inclined to release the petitioner on regular bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above is directed to be released on bail on furnishing of bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court of S.D.J.M., Nagar Untari, Garhwa in connection with Ketar P.S. Case No. 11 of 2024 registered for the offence under Sections 414, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of the I.P.C. and Under Sections 4(1)A and 21 of the Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act subject to the conditions:-
(1) Petitioner shall remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial of this case unless prevented from sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
(2) Petitioner shall not indulge in any or other similar offence till the conclusion of the trial.
(3) Petitioner shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the prosecution witnesses.
In case of violation of the aforesaid conditions, the bail of the petitioner shall be cancelled and shall be taken into custody by the learned Trial Court itself.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Simran Page 2|2 Rambhajan vs The State Of Jharkhand .....
